svg.text: MySQL 8 · InnoDB · 3 entities · PK = primary key, FK = foreign key, UQ = unique, U1/U2 = member of composite UNIQUE key, NN = NOT NULL, CHK = CHECK
One patient has zero or many appointments;
each appointment belongs to exactly one patient.
One doctor has zero or many appointments;
each appointment is with exactly one doctor.
A doctor can never have two appointments at the same date/time. active_flag = 1 while BOOKED and NULL once CANCELLED;
UNIQUE ignores NULLs, so a cancelled row is kept for refund history but no longer blocks the slot (it becomes rebookable).
UNIQUE (patient_id, appt_datetime, active_flag) - a patient cannot be booked twice at the same time
TIME(appt_datetime) BETWEEN '09:00:00' AND '16:30:00' - last slot ends at 17:00
refund_percent IN (0, 50, 100) - the three refund tiers
BOOKED => cancelled_at, refund_percent, refund_amount all NULL; CANCELLED => all three NOT NULL
patient_id -> patients(patient_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT (history is never orphaned)
UNIQUE (email) on patients; CHK chk_doctors_fee: consultation_fee >= 0
Enforced in application code (cannot be a CHECK): bookings must be in the future (NOW() is not allowed in CHECK) and at most 12 BOOKED
appointments per doctor per day (needs a count across rows) - checked inside a transaction that locks the doctor row.
